frames.observation: The exact custom head is readable in settled native snowman_idle as the carved stern face beneath the three-point crown. The head, hat, scarf, middle body and broad glacier base form one intentional stacked silhouette; both articulated crystal hands remain connected. Native HUD elements overlap only the upper crown edge.

A later snowman_idle sample preserves the same complete five-part stack. The head face, crown, scarf, torso, base and hands retain their authored proportions without a sampled mesh explosion or unintended detached surface.

At the telemetry-selected native Attack trigger, the exact head and crown stay aligned while the snowman advances into snowman_attack1. The stacked body and both hands remain readable; the foreground hero and combat slots limit inspection below the scarf.

During snowman_attack1, the custom head tilts with the upper stack and keeps its face and crown coherent. Native blue light and the hero action effect obscure the lower contact area, so this frame supports gross motion rather than fine surface clearance.
The ordinary zero-focus attack begins with Rimecrown intact at HP58. The exact head and crown remain centered above the scarf and body before the native hero action resolves.
During native attack-slot resolution, the face, crown and complete stacked silhouette remain readable. This frame precedes the measured HP transition and does not alone establish hit motion.

The telemetry-selected native Damaged trigger coincides with the bright impact sphere and foreground hero. HP is already descending toward45; the custom head and crown remain visible above the effect, but the effect prevents fine judgment of the middle stack.

The recorded 13-damage label is visible during native snowman_damage. The head and crown lift above the torso while smoke opens between the stacked parts; this matches the controller's deliberate hit reaction rather than an idle binding failure. The hero covers the lower center.

After the hit reaction, camera motion creates transparent afterimages while the exact head and crown return to the intact idle stack at HP45. The model is coherent, but motion blur limits edge inspection.

A later native snowman_attack2 sends the stacked parts upward around a bright ice effect. The selected head renderer remains active, enabled, visible and identity-stable in telemetry, while the top edge and effect prevent complete visual inspection of every airborne part.

The explicit KillSingle capture begins with the exact head and complete five-part Rimecrown intact at HP45. The ordinary hero UI remains visible, but this action is a separate fixture and not ordinary lethal gameplay.

At the exact native Death trigger, the face and crown remain visible above the large impact effect. The effect and hero obscure the lower stack, so this causal frame establishes action provenance rather than fine death-pose quality.

Native snowman_deathDirect is underway with the recorded 1000-damage label. Smoke and upward part travel hide much of the head, while the broad authored base remains visible. This is the controller's animated fall-apart sequence, not a ragdoll.

The broad glacier base remains on the floor as smoke fills the upper target position and the other parts travel away. The exact head renderer is still active, enabled, visible and identity-stable in telemetry, but the image does not provide a clear head-surface view.

The death animation continues with the base clearly visible and upper parts faint or outside the useful camera area. The selected head renderer remains active, enabled, visible and identity-stable by exact telemetry; this frame does not establish a readable corpse or later head position.

The first native loot panel covers the target position. A base edge is visible behind it, but the overlay prevents visual inspection of the exact head. Telemetry still reports the selected head renderer active, enabled, visible and identity-stable; this does not prove a readable corpse.

At the end of the complete 120-frame capture, the loot panel still blocks the target and the base remains partly visible behind it. The selected head renderer remains active, enabled, visible and identity-stable in telemetry, but this sampled handoff does not establish later corpse lifetime or final cleanup.

requirements: All 17 referenced original PNGs were inspected before assigning the reviewed status.
Every observation is scoped to the exact frame and its telemetry boundary.
The ordinary 58 to 45 hit is separate from the explicit 45 to 0 KillSingle fixture.
The source reports m_DoRagdoll false and zero rigidbodies, so the observed fall-apart death is animated and receives no ragdoll credit.
